pr_title: [Fix #13320] Fix incorrect autocorrect when `Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace` and `Style/StringLiterals` autocorrects in the same pass
pr_body:
When both cops are activated and run in the same iteration of the correction loop, `Style/StringLiterals` undoes the moving of spaces that `Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace` performs. This is because `StringLiterals` takes the original string content and transforms it, rather than just modifying the delimiters, in order to handle escaping for quotes within the string.

By marking `Style/StringLiterals` as incompatible with `Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace`, it allows the correction to be deferred to the next inspection loop, thereby avoiding the problem.

Fixes #13320.

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [x] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/
pr_comments: Trying to figure out why this is failing on Windows. For some reason it doesn't detect any `Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace` offenses in the test. 🤔

The Windows failure are due to `create_file` writing files with `'w'` mode, which automatically converts line terminators to the native style. On windows, that's `CRLF`. `Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace` is not set up properly to detect continuations when there's a `\r\n` instead of an `n`.

I updated `create_file` to allow it to force line endings to be retained by using `'wb'` mode instead. We cannot do this across the board because it will cause a lot of `Layout/EndOfLine` failures in other tests, so I made it opt-in.

As a separate PR I am going to look at fixing `Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace` for CRLF line terminators.

There is an issue with the committed code https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/pull/13539/commits/892612b9f85035578a9eb4ddf22422ef0b355c47, which should pass local tests independently, does not. There might be a problem with the procedure for fixing the offense message.
@koic thanks. I had updated the messages in the wrong commit, it's fixed now.

issue_context.title: `Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace` has a autofix logic error
issue_context.body:
## Expected behavior

Describe here how you expected RuboCop to behave in this particular situation.

_Nothing_ - string-splitting is "well defined" at the `\n`, or

```ruby
eq(
  "    0:    1    2    3    4         5    6    7    8      \n    " \
  "8:    9   10   11   12        13   14   15   16      \n   " \
  '16:   17   18   19   20',
)
```

I would also **not force** changing the quotes here. "It doesn't look as pretty here".

## Actual behavior

Describe here what actually happened.
Please use `rubocop --debug` when pasting rubocop output as it contains additional information.

```ruby
eq(
  "    0:    1    2    3    4         5    6    7    8      \n    " \
  "8:    9   10   11   12        13   14   15   16      \n      " \
  '16:   17   18   19   20',
)
```

## Steps to reproduce the problem

This is extremely important! Providing us with a reliable way to reproduce
a problem will expedite its solution.

```ruby
eq(
  "    0:    1    2    3    4         5    6    7    8      \n"\
  "    8:    9   10   11   12        13   14   15   16      \n"\
  "   16:   17   18   19   20"
)
```

## RuboCop version

Include the output of `rubocop -V` or `bundle exec rubocop -V` if using Bundler.
If you see extension cop versions (e.g. `rubocop-performance`, `rubocop-rspec`, and others)
output by `rubocop -V`, include them as well. Here's an example:

```
$ [bundle exec] rubocop -V
1.66.1 (using Parser 3.3.5.0, rubocop-ast 1.32.3, analyzing as Ruby 3.3, running on ruby 3.3.5) [x86_64-linux]
  - rubocop-performance 1.22.1
  - rubocop-rspec 3.1.0
```
comments:
This behavior is the expected behavior for the cop. If this behavior is not desired, the cop should be disabled.
The important issue here is that it belongs to `Layout` department. Considering the formatter expected by the LSP and `rubocop -x`, this should be handled in `Style` department rather than `Layout` department, I think. 
Changing departments would be a breaking change, so it may not be possible to make the change immediately, but the assignment of https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/pull/10715 can be reconsidered.

The

> _Nothing_ - string-splitting is "well defined" at the `\n`,

is "a personal preference of mine". Call it a feature if you want.

I didn't get the exact intrinsics of `Layout` vs `Style` - maybe it is a feature too (and breaking change)

However, autofix **is wrong**:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3596f7e3-34e8-442a-965d-37ab064c4905)

That is a clear bug

If you want this to be understood as a clear bug, you need to change how you report these. Git diffs and unrunnable code snippets are not optimal. Instead show how it changes meaning:

```rb
puts "    0:    1    2    3    4         5    6    7    8      \n    " \
  "8:    9   10   11   12        13   14   15   16      \n      " \
  '16:   17   18   19   20'

    0:    1    2    3    4         5    6    7    8
    8:    9   10   11   12        13   14   15   16
      16:   17   18   19   20

========================================================================

puts   "    0:    1    2    3    4         5    6    7    8      \n"\
  "    8:    9   10   11   12        13   14   15   16      \n"\
  "   16:   17   18   19   20"

    0:    1    2    3    4         5    6    7    8
    8:    9   10   11   12        13   14   15   16
   16:   17   18   19   20
```

Indentation output changes.

If I had just reported the string, then the indentation, given the `\` would've already disoriented the reader.

And if I wrote a whole `rspec` for it (hence the `eq`), it would not have been a _MWE_ from a repro standpoint.
I didn't know that there was a **requirement** for the code to be _executable_ - just valid Ruby

Feel free to change the description @Earlopain. But **not** delete the history of edits, though.

All of the autofix bugs I have opened so far have been dealt in about 1d-2d time.

Is this perhaps forgotten @koic? 🙏

FYI, the following configuration would probably give you the behaviour you're looking for here (keep string quotes consistent in a multiline string, and put spaces at the beginning of a string instead of the end in a continuation):

```yaml
Style/StringLiterals:
  ConsistentQuotesInMultiline: true

Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace:
  EnforcedStyle: leading
```

> FYI, the following configuration would probably give you the behaviour you're looking for here (keep string quotes consistent in a multiline string, and put spaces at the beginning of a string instead of the end in a continuation):
> 
> ```yaml
> Style/StringLiterals:
>   ConsistentQuotesInMultiline: true
> 
> Layout/LineContinuationLeadingSpace:
>   EnforcedStyle: leading
> ```

Eeeh ... I'd have to evaluate what changes either does, if I really get into it.

Yes, in this case leading spaces would be best (and assuming `\n` is **not** considered space). But maybe the default looks better in other places.

This will probably be one disable I won't remove (if I was going to merge rubocop, which won't be happening apparently) - unless the block-style disable gets flagged as useless.

Thank you for looking into it / figuring it out. It drove me crazy "how on earth" this could be a problem.
I guess after having seen my recent issues and fixes I sort-of gotten an experience on "what is at fault" usually.
